title: Lefamulin versus moxifloxacin in community-acquired bacterial pneumonia
topic_state: POOLED -- risk ratio, k=2, registry-sourced throughout
verification_basis: Both registrations read from ClinicalTrials.gov on 2026-08-18: conditions, arm groups with types, registered primary outcome measures, and the POSTED RESULTS counts and denominators used in the pool.
provenance: REGISTRY THROUGHOUT. Every count and denominator in this pool is read from ClinicalTrials.gov posted results. No publication figure is used and no value is imported.

primary.comparator: moxifloxacin (with or without linezolid in LEAP 1)

pooled_hartung_knapp.why_it_is_shown: Handbook 6.5 section 10.10.4.5 recommends the Hartung-Knapp adjustment where k is small. At k=2 it uses t on ONE degree of freedom, whose critical value is 12.71 against the normal 1.96, so the interval is very much wider. IT IS SHOWN ALONGSIDE RATHER THAN INSTEAD, because presenting only the narrow interval would overstate what two trials establish and presenting only the wide one would understate two large concordant trials. A floor of 1 is applied to the variance-inflation factor so the adjustment can never NARROW the interval below the unadjusted one.

heterogeneity.how_to_read_this_at_k2: I-squared and tau-squared at k=2 are WEAK evidence about consistency in either direction. Two points cannot demonstrate agreement, and a low value here means only that the two estimates are CONSISTENT WITH a common effect -- not that one is established.
heterogeneity.tau2_estimator: REML -- copied from this block's declared `estimator`, which is the authoritative record of how the pool was computed. NOT inferred: an object that declared no estimator would be left undeclared here, because the absence is itself the finding.
heterogeneity.i2_definition: UNDECIDABLE from this object. I-squared is 0 and Q is below the degrees of freedom, where the Higgins form is negative-and-clamped and the REML/metafor form is exactly zero -- BOTH DEFINITIONS GIVE 0 and nothing here distinguishes them. Recorded as undecidable rather than guessed.

per_trial.label: LEAP 1
per_trial.how: RR = (e1/n1)/(e2/n2); SE(log RR) = sqrt(1/e1 - 1/n1 + 1/e2 - 1/n2), Handbook 6.5 section 6.4.1. The COUNTS are read from the registry's posted results; only the arithmetic is ours and the formula is shown so both can be checked.

per_trial.label: LEAP 2
per_trial.how: RR = (e1/n1)/(e2/n2); SE(log RR) = sqrt(1/e1 - 1/n1 + 1/e2 - 1/n2), Handbook 6.5 section 6.4.1. The COUNTS are read from the registry's posted results; only the arithmetic is ours and the formula is shown so both can be checked.

primary.denominator_handling: LEAP 1 posts responder / non-responder / INDETERMINATE, summing exactly to the denominator (241+29+6=276; 248+21+6=275). LEAP 2 posts responder / non-responder only, leaving 5 and 3 participants unaccounted against its posted denominators (336+29=365 of 370; 334+31=365 of 368). THE POSTED DENOMINATOR IS USED IN BOTH, so non-response and indeterminacy are treated alike as not-responding. For a comparison against an ACTIVE control that is the conservative direction: it cannot flatter the experimental arm.
primary.why_this_topic_pools_when_most_do_not: Of 62 infectious-disease topics, this is one of the few that survives all four limbs without reconciliation: the SAME experimental drug in the experimental arm of both trials, the SAME active comparator, the SAME registered primary outcome measured the same way, and the SAME infection. The eleven topics closed on 2026-08-18 failed because one of those four differed. This is what a poolable topic looks like.

published_synthesis_comparison.status: NOT DONE -- recorded as owed rather than claimed
published_synthesis_comparison.what_is_owed: A published meta-analysis or regulatory review pooling these two trials on this outcome has NOT been searched for or read. Until it is, this object states an estimate that has not been checked against anyone else's. That is a gap in this page, and it is named here rather than left for a reader to discover.
published_synthesis_comparison.why_it_matters_here: Both trial pairs are registration trials for a new antibiotic, so a regulatory review almost certainly pools them and would be the strongest available comparator.

primary.what_this_does_not_establish: NOT that either trial is free of bias -- NO RISK-OF-BIAS ASSESSMENT IS RECORDED, and a pooled estimate without one is an arithmetic result, not a graded finding. NOT non-inferiority or superiority: both trials were designed as non-inferiority studies against an active comparator, and a risk ratio near 1 with an interval spanning 1 is the EXPECTED result of a successful non-inferiority trial rather than evidence of no difference. NOT that the pooled interval is reliable at k=2 -- see the Hartung-Knapp interval, which is the honest width. NOT agreement with any published synthesis; none has been checked.

handbook_authority.handbook: Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions
handbook_authority.estimator_note: REML is the Handbook 6.5 default tau-squared estimator. At k=2 the Handbook notes that random-effects estimates of between-study variance are very imprecise, and 10.10.4.5 recommends the Hartung-Knapp adjustment where k is small.

POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.a_the_analysis_population_was_checked_an: CHECKED AND CLEAN. Read from the registrations on 2026-08-21: NCT02559310 registers 'Early Clinical Response (ECR)' (population: ECR); NCT02813694 registers 'Early Clinical Response (ECR)' (population: ECR). Both trials register the same primary in the same population, so this pool does NOT cross an analysis-population boundary. Recorded because a check that only speaks when it finds something cannot be told from a check that was never run.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.b_what_remains_unresolved: Whether these are non-inferiority designs is NOT established: the registration fields fetched do not use the word, and a pooled ratio from non-inferiority trials answers a different question from a superiority pool. Unresolved, not assumed.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.a_the_two_trials_differ_in_route_and_dur: THE EXPERIMENTAL ARMS ARE NOT THE SAME INTERVENTION. Read from the pooled analysis (PMID 33964925, BMC Pulm Med 2021): LEAP 1 randomised patients to INTRAVENOUS lefamulin 150 mg every 12 hours for 5-7 days with an OPTIONAL INTRAVENOUS-TO-ORAL SWITCH; LEAP 2 randomised to ORAL lefamulin 600 mg every 12 hours for 5 days. THIS OBJECT POOLS THEM AS ONE INTERVENTION.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.b_and_the_comparators_differ_as_this_obj: LEAP 1's comparator is moxifloxacin WITH OR WITHOUT LINEZOLID and LEAP 2's is moxifloxacin alone -- corroborated from the registered arm groups. This object's own question already states the comparator difference; THE ROUTE AND DURATION DIFFERENCE WAS NOT PREVIOUSLY RECORDED.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.c_what_is_not_claimed: NOT that the pool is invalid -- an intravenous-to-oral switch and an oral course of the same drug are a defensible thing to combine, and the published analysis combines them. What is claimed is that a reader meeting one ratio should know the two arms differed in route, duration and comparator, and no field said so.

r_output._what_this_is: The console output of the fit, captured as it was printed. NOT re-typed and NOT summarised -- P46 limb 4 asks for the model output, and a paraphrase of model output is a claim about a model rather than the model's own words.
r_output.call: rma(yi = yi, sei = sei, method = "REML")  and the same fit with test = "knha"
r_output.inputs_derivation: yi = log(point); sei = (log(ci_high) - log(ci_low)) / (2 * 1.959964). Read from this object's own per_trial rows. NO COUNT IS INVENTED and no interval is re-typed.
r_output.hartung_knapp_note: Shown BESIDE the unadjusted interval, never instead of it. At k = 2 the t critical value is 12.7062 on 1 degree of freedom, which is why the adjusted interval is very wide -- that width is the honest one at this k.
r_output.what_k_equals_2_means: Two trials cannot inform a between-study variance. tau^2 is estimated with ONE degree of freedom and Q on 1 df carries almost no information about heterogeneity. THAT IS A PROPERTY OF THE EVIDENCE -- there are two trials -- and not of our access to it.
r_output.interval_method: REML with the unadjusted Wald interval, and the same fit under Hartung-Knapp beside it. The eleven topics closed on 2026-08-18 failed because one of those four differed. This is what a poolable topic looks like.

primary.what_this_does_not_establish: NOT that either trial is free of bias -- NO RISK-OF-BIAS ASSESSMENT IS RECORDED, and a pooled estimate without one is an arithmetic result, not a graded finding. steps.reason: Both results are SOME_CONCERNS. D1, D4 and D5 are LOW on read registrations -- randomised, QUADRUPLE masking INCLUDING the outcomes assessor, and a single registered primary that is the one pooled -- but D2 and D3 are NO_INFORMATION because the registrations do not carry deviation or missing-data fields. An unjudgeable domain caps the overall at SOME_CONCERNS.

The stored refit gives tau^2 EXACTLY ZERO, Q 0.7316 on 1 df, p = 0.3924. The two intervals -- 0.9683 (0.9123 to 1.0276) and 1.0006 (0.9556 to 1.0476) -- overlap almost entirely and agree in conclusion. Downgrading here would manufacture a caution the numbers do not support.

Early Clinical Response is the SINGLE registered primary on both trials and is exactly what is pooled. RECORDED AND NOT USED TO DOWNGRADE: LEAP 1's comparator is moxifloxacin WITH OR WITHOUT LINEZOLID and LEAP 2's is moxifloxacin alone. The object discloses this in its own question, and the endpoint definition is unaffected by it, so it is stated rather than converted into a rating.

k = 2. The Hartung-Knapp interval is RR 0.9884 (0.7807 to 1.2513 -- and NOT 0.8079 to 1.2093, which is metafor's RAW unfloored knha interval) on t = 12.7062 with 1 df -- wide enough to include both a meaningful benefit and a meaningful harm. Two trials cannot inform a between-study variance, and no optimal information size is recorded on this object.

primary.summary: LOW certainty. The two trials agree closely and the endpoint is the registered primary assessed under quadruple masking, so the downgrades are for unread deviation and missing-data domains and for k = 2, not for inconsistency or indirectness.

Read from the pooled analysis (PMID 33964925, BMC Pulm Med 2021): LEAP 1 randomised patients to INTRAVENOUS lefamulin 150 mg every 12 hours for 5-7 days with an OPTIONAL INTRAVENOUS-TO-ORAL SWITCH; LEAP 2 randomised to ORAL lefamulin 600 mg every 12 hours for 5 days. THIS OBJECT POOLS THEM AS ONE INTERVENTION. LEAP 1's comparator is moxifloxacin WITH OR WITHOUT LINEZOLID and LEAP 2's is moxifloxacin alone -- corroborated from the registered arm groups. This object's own question already states the comparator difference; THE ROUTE AND DURATION DIFFERENCE WAS NOT PREVIOUSLY RECORDED. NOT that the pool is invalid -- an intravenous-to-oral switch and an oral course of the same drug are a defensible thing to combine, and the published analysis combines them. What is claimed is that a reader meeting one ratio should know the two arms differed in route, duration and comparator, and no field said so.

manuscript.introduction:
This review asks: In Lefamulin versus moxifloxacin in community-acquired bacterial pneumonia, what is the effect on versus moxifloxacin (with or without linezolid in LEAP 1) on early clinical response?

It pools 2 randomised trials, against moxifloxacin (with or without linezolid in LEAP 1).

The outcome pooled is early clinical response.

Every count and denominator behind those estimates is read as follows. REGISTRY THROUGHOUT. Every count and denominator in this pool is read from ClinicalTrials.gov posted results. No publication figure is used and no value is imported.

Everything in this paragraph is derived from stored fields and none of it is authored. The interpretive sentences that follow are marked as drafts and are the author's to replace.

bookkeeping_2026_08_21._what: The five reporting claims a PRISMA-2020 manuscript needs that are FETCHABLE rather than argued -- each derived from a field here, or stated as an honest absence.
bookkeeping_2026_08_21.which_limbs_this_review_refuses: Of the four properties this project requires of a completed topic, 4 are held (comparison denominator, grade per pool, model output verbatim, rob per result).
bookkeeping_2026_08_21.the_search_its_date_and_its_databases: PRIMARY TRIALS. NO BIBLIOGRAPHIC SEARCH FOR PRIMARY TRIALS WAS RUN. The 2 included trials were identified by reading named registrations on 2026-08-18. Both registrations read from ClinicalTrials.gov on 2026-08-18: conditions, arm groups with types, registered primary outcome measures, and the POSTED RESULTS counts and denominators used in the pool. PUBLISHED SYNTHESES. PubMed E-utilities esearch + esummary, executed 2026-08-21. Query as executed: (lefamulin[tiab]) AND (meta-analysis[pt] OR "systematic review"[pt] OR meta-analysis[tiab] OR "pooled"[tiab] OR LEAP[tiab]). It matched 19 record(s), of which 19 were retrieved and 19 read; 1 appraised.
bookkeeping_2026_08_21.whether_this_review_was_prospectively_re: NO PROSPERO REGISTRATION OR PROTOCOL RECORD IS HELD ON THIS OBJECT. That is not the same as knowing this review was not registered, and neither claim is made. It is recorded here as an absence so that a reader does not have to infer it from silence.
bookkeeping_2026_08_21.that_two_assessors_disagreed_and_where: Risk of bias was assessed independently a second time by GPT-5 Codex (openai family), via `codex exec`, blind to this assessment and given the same registry facts. 4 of 12 judgements -- 33.3%. Reported as DISAGREEMENT: agreement between two assessors given the same facts authenticates nothing. By domain: D1 2 of 2 disagree, D2 0 of 2 disagree, D3 0 of 2 disagree, D4 0 of 2 disagree, D5 0 of 2 disagree, OVERALL 2 of 2 disagree. Recounted after this review's D1 judgements moved: 2 of 12 judgements -- 16.7%.

They are kept under this dated key, each marked `is_a_draft`, so a later pass can always tell what was written from what was read. A draft must never quietly become a fact.
manuscript_draft_2026_08_21._the_rule: No drafted sentence asserts anything this object cannot back. Where the claim requires a judgement, the draft stops at the facts and says so. A plausible sentence is the one most likely to survive dictation unexamined, which is why none is written.
